headline: Structured drug-target knowledge resources paired with computational discovery workflows
label: Curated Biological Knowledge Resources
summary: Three January 2026 items pair curated drug-target resources with network and neural discovery workflows.
synthesis: The common thread is the organization of drug, target, and mechanism data into linked, queryable representations. NavDB provides an open-access resource of 8023 curated records covering 5168 voltage-gated sodium channel modulators and targets, with search and peptide matching functions. The Ayurvedic herbal study constructs a knowledge graph and network-pharmacology pipeline to map multi-target mechanisms of single herbal drugs in diabetes and obesity. The third item applies a fragment-based neural network to propose JAK2 and GLP-1R drug candidates and to map clinically relevant drug-target interactomes through in silico binding analysis. What is distinctive is the pairing of curated, searchable resources with discovery workflows operating on target-centric relationships, though only the first two items are resource-oriented.
